transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-10
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (SummitPay), Ravi Patel (SummitPay), Marta Ruiz (SummitPay), Omar Haddad (SummitPay)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Alex with Redwood, with me is Priya and Daniel. Quick agenda: show structured output JSON mode, function/tool calling, how console ties into Optimize, and leave time for security questions.
[00:22] Laura: Great, thanks. We're excited to see how the structured output can help our payments pipeline. We get messy OCR and want the model to emit strict JSON so our downstream jobs ingest without extra parsing.
[00:35] Priya: Yep that's exactly where the JSON mode shines. We'll show schema enforcement and guardrails so you get deterministic keys back. Quick question on dataset size, Laura how many receipts/payments per day?
[00:50] Laura: Right now roughly 200k events, spikes up to 1M during promos, so throughput matters. Latency target is <200ms 95p for live UX.
[01:10] Ravi: We also have strict PII rules, data must not be stored outside our VPC; exploring private deployment or dedicated capacity.
[01:28] Alex: Understood, we'll cover deployment options — hosted for quick starts, Dedicated for isolated pools, and Private for VPC/on-prem. We'll call out tradeoffs on cost/latency.
[01:45] Priya: Jumping into the demo — starting with API quickstart, here is a sample request using JSON mode. (screen share)
[02:10] Priya: Example schema: required fields transaction_id, amount, currency, merchant_name, timestamp. We set strict:true so extra keys get rejected and you get a validation error instead of fuzzy output.
[02:40] Omar: If validation fails do you return an error code or try to autocorrect?
[02:55] Priya: The runtime returns a structured validation error by default. You can also set a fallback handler that triggers a function call to a sanitization tool we can register — that's function-calling.
[03:20] Daniel: Quick note — sometimes the transcription will refer to KV "cash"; we mean KV cache for token caching, sorry for any confusions on earlier docs.
[03:40] Ravi: How do you enforce the schema in the model vs post-validate? We need guarantees the model won't hallucinate fields like customer_ssn.
[03:55] Priya: We have two layers: first, schema-guided decoding in the model that biases generation to the schema shape; second, server-side strict validation. Also guardrails allow blocking patterns (e.g., regex to reject SSN-like tokens) and redaction hooks before logging.
[04:30] Marta: Speaking of logging, what about audit logs and who can see inference payloads? We need KMS integration and ability to purge logs.
[04:45] Alex: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS, audit logs with retention controls, and RBAC in the Console. We'll send the SOC2 whitepaper and KMS integration guide after the call.
[05:10] Priya: Back to function-calling — we'll demo a flow where the model returns a JSON payload and then calls an internal "normalize_merchant" function. That function is defined in the Console and has a typed schema.
[05:35] [screen share] Priya: Here's a live example: model returns {"transaction_id": "T-12345", "amount": 12.50, "currency": "USD"} then triggers function: normalize_merchant({"merchant_name": "Starbuxx"})
[06:10] Laura: Nice, can we run custom functions that call our internal enrichment service behind the VPC?
[06:25] Priya: For Dedicated/Private yes. For hosted we provide secure tool calling endpoints with customer-managed auth; for VPC/on-prem we can attach function runners to your network.
[06:45] Ravi: Latency impact for an extra function call? If the model calls a function synchronously that could add 50-200ms depending on your service. That's where routing and cache strategies matter.
[07:05] Daniel: Optimize can recommend batching and caching settings to hit your cost/latency SLOs. For example, prefix caching of repetitive merchant names drops token compute significantly.
[07:30] Priya: Demo of the Console: route config, per-route model pinning, structured-output toggle, and guardrail rules. (navigates) You can attach a schema via upload or pointing to an S3/URL.
[08:10] Omar: Are schemas versioned? We need backward compatibility when we change output shape.
[08:22] Priya: Yes, Console supports schema versioning and can route traffic to different schema versions in canary rollouts. Also supports automatic regression checks against a prompt test set.
[08:45] Laura: If the model regresses on quality after quantization, do you alert?
[09:00] Priya: Optimize monitors quality metrics tied to eval prompt sets. You can set regression thresholds to trigger rollbacks or notify engineers.
[09:18] Ravi: On the topic of quantization — we ran internal tests with 8-bit weights but saw some entity extraction errors. How do you recommend balancing model size vs extraction fidelity?
[09:40] Daniel: Our suggestion is hybrid: keep critical routes on higher-precision weights and batch/quantize auxiliary routes. Optimize gives per-route quantization suggestions and historical evals.
[10:05] [11:00] Priya: Now i'll show a JSON-mode guardrail: regex denylist for PII, plus an allowlist for currency codes. if a currency isn't on allowlist the request is flagged.
[11:30] Ravi: What about streaming responses with structured output? We need partial output for long documents.
[11:45] Priya: We stream tokens but structured streaming is tricky; we support chunked JSON emission plus intermediate validation checkpoints. For long OCR jobs we recommend chunking documents and reassembling validated objects.
[12:10] Omar: Any limits on schema complexity? Deeply nested schemas or arrays?
[12:25] Priya: Supported but watch performance; deeply nested validation will add overhead. We often flatten for throughput-sensitive pipelines.
[12:50] Laura: Are there any hard guarantees that the model won't add unexpected fields? We need determinism for downstream jobs.
[13:05] Priya: With strict schema enforcement + server-side rejection you get deterministic outputs: if the model tries to output an extra field the call returns a validation error and you can trigger a fallback function to attempt a normalized response.
[13:35] [15:00] Alex: Switching gears — integration and PoC. Typical PoC we do is 2-4 weeks with a small sample set, dedicated capacity trial or hosted spike depending on privacy needs.
[15:20] Laura: We prefer dedicated trial first, then expand to Private if we need VPC binding.
[15:35] Alex: Understood. We'll propose Dedicated baseline in the worksheet.
[15:50] Omar: Security — can we bring our own KMS and have keys never leave our control?
[16:05] Marta: Also SSO and SCIM?
[16:18] Alex: Yes to both. Private & Dedicated support customer-managed KMS and SAML/SCIM-based provisioning. We'll attach the security integration guide.
[16:35] Priya: Quick demo of function-calling tool registry: you can declare function schema in the Console, set permissions, and test-run it against sample payloads.
[16:55] Priya: Example: function normalize_merchant returns canonical id and category. In our demo run the model calls it and the function returns enrichment.
[17:20] Ravi: If the function fails do you retry? semantics?
[17:35] Daniel: You can configure retry policies and fallbacks. There's also dead-lettering for failed function calls and observability in Console logs.
[18:00] Laura: Observability — how deep are the traces? We need token-level latency for billing reconciliation.
[18:12] Alex: Console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency histograms, and trace IDs you can join with your logs. We can also forward telemetry to your Datadog or Splunk.
[18:40] Omar: Are req/res payloads stored in cleartext in hosted mode? What's redaction?
[18:55] Priya: Hosted mode stores payloads encrypted at rest; we redact based on patterns and can disable retention. For highest control use Private.
[19:20] [20:00] Priya: Live QA — i'll run a quick sample where the model is asked to extract fields from an OCR blob. (runs) We get a valid JSON and the function call to normalize merchant succeeded.
[20:30] [screen shows latency metrics] Priya: This run was 180ms 95p using a mid-tier model with prefix caching. Without caching it was 320ms.
[20:55] Ravi: Good to know. What about cost per 1k transactions for that throughput?
[21:10] Alex: We'll send the pricing worksheet that includes per-token and per-embedding math and a dedicated capacity estimate. Pricing will vary by model family and quantization.
[21:40] Omar: Are there pre-built connectors to common enterprise systems? e.g., SFTP, Kafka, or our internal enrichment bus?
[21:55] Daniel: We provide connectors and you can plug functions into your bus; for private deployments we can run function runners in your VPC.
[22:20] Laura: For acceptance criteria — we need >= 95% field extraction accuracy on our test set and sustained latency <200ms 95p.
[22:40] Priya: We'll use your test set during PoC and set up the eval harness in Console to run nightly regressions.
[23:00] [25:00] Marta: A few compliance asks: SOC2 scope, data residency controls (EU), and if you support customer-specific redaction policies.
[23:20] Alex: We'll include SOC2 docs, and our Private deployment supports regional tenancy. Redaction policies are configurable per-route.
[23:45] Ravi: For function calling auth to our internal services, do you support mTLS or token exchange?
[23:58] Daniel: Both; we support mutual TLS and token-based auth. We can walk your infra team through the wiring during the PoC.
[24:30] Priya: Quick note on failure modes — sometimes model outputs malformed JSON due to tokenization. Our SDKs include helpers to sanitize and attempt a second pass; but with strict mode we prefer rejecting and triggering a function to correct.
[25:05] Laura: That works. What about rate limits? We'll be ingesting bursts during promos.
[25:20] Alex: Dedicated pools handle bursting with reserved capacity and burst credit; autoscaling policies can be tuned in Console.
[25:50] Omar: Do you have SLA language for latency/uptime?
[26:05] Alex: Yes Dedicated includes SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll share the SLA doc. Hosted has best-effort but we provide SLOs and high-availability regions.
[26:30] Priya: Another feature — structured output with function-calling can be combined with reranking. E.g., generate candidate merchant matches then call a function to pick best canonical id.
[27:00] Laura: Could that reduce our false-positive merchant merges?
[27:14] Priya: Exactly, reranking + enrichment functions are a common pattern.
[27:40] [30:00] Priya: Walkthrough of Optimize recommendations: per-route batching, quantization suggestion, and cost/latency tradeoff sliders in Console. You can simulate cost impact before applying.
[30:30] Ravi: Any automated guardrails to prevent a rollout that increases latency?
[30:45] Priya: Canary rollouts plus automatic rollback on regression thresholds. You can also set manual approval gates.
[31:10] Omar: On-boarding timeline? If we sign, how soon can we start a PoC?
[31:25] Alex: Typically within 1-2 weeks for hosted or dedicated trial; private deployments take longer due to infra.
[31:40] Laura: We want start week of Apr 20.
[31:50] Alex: We'll tentatively schedule PoC kickoff and send calendar invite.
[32:05] [35:00] Priya: Final demo snippet — show error path where model tries to add a "ssn" field; strict mode rejects and triggers a sanitization function that redacts candidate sequences and returns an error that you can surface to product.
[35:30] Marta: Good. We also need to ensure logs are segmented so auditors only see meta-level results.
[35:50] Alex: We support role-based log views and retention segmentation.
[36:10] Ravi: One more question: Are there built-in eval suites for common tasks like entity extraction so we don't start from scratch?
[36:25] Priya: Yes, Console has templates and you can import evaluation suites; we can also help bootstrap evals as part of Solutions Eng engagement.
[36:50] Laura: Ok let's wrap with a recap and next steps.
[37:05] Alex: Recap: we'll send pricing, Dedicated sizing worksheet, SOC2/KMS guide, JSON schema examples, and schedule PoC kickoff for week of Apr 20. PoC success criteria: 95% extraction accuracy + <200ms 95p latency.
[37:30] Laura: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[37:45] Omar: Thanks, recording please?
[37:50] Alex: Yes we'll share recording and slide deck.
[38:00] [end of recording]

Notes on transcript quality: occasional transcription errors and speaker attribution imperfect (e.g., Daniel sometimes labeled as Speaker 3). Some technical terms transcribed incorrectly (KV cash instead of KV cache).
